'''''Cestrum aurantiacum'''''<ref>[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=CEAU2 ''Cestrum aurantiacum''] at [https://plants.usda.gov/ USDA PLANTS Database]</ref> ('''orange cestrum''', '''"[[orange jessamine]]"''', '''orange-flowering jessamine''', and '''yellow cestrum''';<ref>[http://www.sntc.org.sz/alienplants/speciesinfo.asp?spid=127 ''Cestrum aurantiacum''] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930193534/http://www.sntc.org.sz/alienplants/speciesinfo.asp?spid=127 |date=September 30, 2007 }} at [http://www.sntc.org.sz/flora/index.asp Swaziland's Flora Database] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070713172017/http://www.sntc.org.sz/flora/index.asp |date=July 13, 2007 }}</ref> [[syn.]] ''Capraria lanceolata'' L.f.) is a species of shrub in the potato family [[Solanaceae]] that is native to tropical regions of [[North America|North]] and [[South America]].

==Description==
[[File: Cestrum aurantiacum 1.jpg|thumb|left|Large shrubby plant]]
Cestrum aurantiacum is a shrub 1.5 to 6.5 m tall or occasionally up to 8.5 m tall. The branches are glabrous or sparsely [[tomentose]]. The leaves are [[Glossary of botanical terms|ovate]] to elliptical, 7 to 17 cm long and 2.5 to 5.5 cm wide. Both sides of the leaf are [[glabrous]], the tip is acuminate or shortly tapering, the base is acuminate to blunt or occasionally shortly tapering. The [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]]s are 1 to 3 cm long and glabrous.<ref name=NParks/>

===Inflorescences=== 
The terminal or axillary, umbelliferous or [[racemose]] inflorescences consist of a few to a few flowers. The inflorescence axis is finely hairy or hairless, the [[bracts]] linear and later [[deciduous]]. The flowers are [[Sessility (botany)|sessile]], almost sessile or stand on flower stalks up to 1.5 mm long. [[Free-flowering|Blooming constantly]] through the year, the flowers produce a [[citrus]]-like scent at night.<ref name=NParks>[https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/3/6/3666#:~:text=Flowers%20produce%20a%20citrus%2Dlike,throughout%20most%20of%20the%20year.&text=Fruits%20are%20small%2C%20round%2C%20white%20berries. Cestrum aurantiacum Lindl.] by [[National Parks Board]]. Retrieved January 31, 2025.</ref>

The [[Sepal|calyx]] is tubular, 5 to 6.5 (rarely up to 9) mm long and hairless except for the (0.7) 1 to 2 (3) mm long, ciliate calyx lobes. These are awl-shaped and long-spiked or rounded and long-spiked and run further down the calyx tube as five nerve tracts.

[[File:Cestrum aurantiacum-fruits-2-yercaud-salem-India.JPG|thumb|left|White berries]]
The orange or rarely yellow [[Perianth|corolla]] has a 17.5 to 20 mm long corolla tube, the corolla lobes are 3 to 3.5 (5.5) mm long, egg-shaped or lanceolate. The edges are covered with [[papillose]] hairs. The [[stamen]]s are 4 to 6.5 mm long, swollen and bent over in a knee-like shape, groove-like or almost appendage-like. The base and the vascular bundles of the stamens are hairy. The [[Style (botany)|style]] is 16.5 to 18.5 mm long.<ref>Johnnie L. Gentry Jr. and Paul Standley: Flora of Guatemala. Solanaceae, Fieldiana:Botany, Volume 24, Part X, Numbers 1 and 2. Field Museum of Natural History, 1974.</ref>

The fruits are white [[berries]] (which are distinguished from the black fruits of ''[[Cestrum parqui]]''), 8 to 12 mm long, with seven to nine seeds, which are about 3 to 5 mm long.<ref name=NParks/>

==Distribution==
This species is distributed in an area extending from southern [[Mexico]] to [[Nicaragua]], where it is found in moist [[thicket]]s or forests, often in pine-oak forests at altitudes between 1000 and 2600 m.<ref name=NParks/>

==Cultivation==
[[File:Cestrum aurantiacum - Orange Cestrum at Ooty 2014 (17).jpg|thumb|Foliage and flowers]]
This plant is used as an [[ornamental plant]], and it is a [[poisonous plant]] if eaten by animals.<ref>{{GRIN | accessdate = 16 January 2018}}</ref> However, the species is widely grown as an [[ornamental plant]] and in some places it has [[escaped plant|escaped from cultivation]] and returned to the wild. In parts of Africa, Asia and Australia, the species has become a harmful invasive species. The top of the plant is [[plant hardiness|hardy]] to zone 8 but it is root hardy to zone 7.<ref>[https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/cestrum-aurantiacum/ Cestrum aurantiacum] by [[NC State University]]. Retrieved January 31, 2025.</ref>

[[Drought tolerant]], the species grows best in occasionally moist, [[humus]]-rich, well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade. The size of the shrub is easily controlled by [[pruning]]. It is regarded as medicinal in Peru. The flowers attract hummingbirds, butterflies, and other pollinating insects.<ref>[http://www.wnsstamps.post/en/stamps/PE065.07 ''Cestrum aurantiacum''] at Universal Postal Union - stamps of Peru]</ref>
